beur-hagra/1:_: Seif 1 on Chanukah and Purim etc. — meaning: even though we say in the first chapter of Rosh Hashanah that the days of Chanukah and Purim did not annul Megillat Taanit, that refers to the days themselves, therefore we fast on the 13th of Adar. See there. We need not say this for Purim since it is divrei kabbalah etc. as written there 19a; and what Megillah 5 says "was not needed" etc. — meaning for eulogy and fasting they are Purim days for everyone, and one might think even for melacha they are for everyone, but because of before and after them not — therefore he asked because of after them; even before, if something occurred and Nicanor's day was annulled as in Taanit 18a, and Mordechai in the name of Rabbati who wrote that from what we include them in Yerushalmi — they said on all we fast except Shabbat, Yom Tov, Rosh Chodesh, Chanukah and Purim — all are equal; so in Razah and Ran Taanit ch. 2; even though Yerushalmi says also before Purim to forbid because of the day before it — Yerushalmi argues with gemara and holds divrei kabbalah are not like Torah law; see Tosafot there 18a s.v. Rav etc. Rif disagrees in the first chapter of Megillah and forbids before and after; nevertheless before Purim he wrote forbidden only for eulogy alone, reason being Fast of Esther; he wrote there: even though R' Yochanan ruled like R' Meir not to eulogize, we do not rule like them since Rav Ashi says there "all that is after it" etc. — he is like R' Yosi, and therefore here in Shulchan Aruch before and after. But Ran in Taanit ch. 2 rules like R' Yochanan. Rif's words in Megillah there require study — he wrote forbidden before and after in eulogy, which is not like Rav Ashi; Yerushalmi challenges on Nicanor's day that it is not itself because it is the day before the 14th and answers to inform you it is forbidden in eulogy; Ran brought it in Taanit there — it appears these are not Rif's words; Ran likewise there.
baer-heitev/2:ד: (ד) To eat — meaning even more than ten. And Taz wrote one should not rely on this gloss but should eat the milah feast at night as in siman 472 see there. When Adar enters we increase in joy. One who has a lawsuit with a gentile should judge it in Adar. R' Moshe Alshekar siman 41 wrote the townspeople may enact with agreement and cherem upon them and those coming after them to make Purim for a miracle done to them, and even if they go to another city to settle it applies to them; and one for whom a miracle occurred in Adar and vowed to make Purim for him — some say to do it in a leap year in second Adar and some say in first Adar unless the miracle occurred in the leap year in second Adar — R' Shimshon Levi siman 16; and see what is written siman 568 seif 7 (and Magen Avraham disagrees; and in Eliyah Rabbah he rejected his words in siman 685 see there). Knesset HaGedolah wrote: one who fasts on the day a miracle was done to him and it occurs on Shabbat — he fasts on erev Shabbat.
beer-hagolah/3:_: Tur in the name of Mesechet Soferim — and even though those days were in Nisan they did not want to fast in Nisan because our ancestors were redeemed in it and the Mishkan was established.
kaf-hachayyim/2:_: (ב) There. It is permitted to fast before them etc., and likewise permitted to eulogize before them and after them. Rambam ch. 11 Laws of Mourning. Beit Yosef. And see below siman 696 seif 3 and in our words there b'siyata dishmaya.
peri-megadim/1:_: Permitted — Taz omitted eulogy; see Tur who questioned before them and after them and Beit Yosef; and difficult — Rav and R' Yehuda, halacha is like R' Yehuda, and Peri Chadash here — if so only before it would be forbidden; and possible specifically when he divides — halacha is like R' Yehuda — not so here perhaps he said so Peri Chadash. And what he wrote regarding this matter "was annulled" etc. — this answers Tur see there who wrote Tur and there is support from gemara like Rabbenu Tam and per this there is no answer to this — for in gemara days Megillat Taanit was not yet annulled Beit Yosef; and must say Tur means Chanukah — reason Megillat Taanit was annulled before and after; and what he said 13th was not needed is a verse — reason of answer of Razah z"l in Beit Yosef divrei kabbalah and is like Torah law and no strengthening and they did not forbid at all before and after on Purim; however for sons of 14th it is not kabbalah to forbid them the 15th except Megillat Taanit to forbid one from the other — if so forbidden as Peri Chadash wrote regarding walled cities forbidden on 13th since answer of Razah z"l does not apply — 14th for walled cities is not kabbalah as written in Megillah walled cities on 15th see there. And see Razah and one can say forbidden after it; see Levush and we hold like Tur. In another explanation Taz and must say "was annulled" for Chanukah and Purim and in Diharan printing corrected well. And in our innovations we wrote if a surrounded village has an entry day — and per Rabbenu Tam per his method it has none as Tosafot 3b s.v. walled city.
yad-ephraim/2:_: In Taz s.k. 2 — because one cannot delay until day one per explanation one does not establish it on erev Shabbat etc., as should be read.
machatzit-hashekel/3:ג: (3) And in Hagahot Maimoniyot: even on Purim etc., as in Megillah 7a — R' Eliezer was sitting before Rav Kahana on Purim; it was evening and the rabbis did not come to the beit midrash, and Rav Kahana said: why did the rabbis not come? They said: perhaps they are busy with the Purim feast. He said: is it not possible for them to eat at night (i.e. the night of the 14th)? He said: the Master does not hold like Rava who said: a Purim feast eaten at night did not fulfill etc. — it implies that in other years their way was to come before their rabbi even on Purim; from his asking why they did not come etc. And in Sefer Avodat Yisrael he wondered: for it is explicit in Maharil the reason is because they are busy, and what he wrote that Esther does not teach is only a hint; therefore he wrote that if one has someone to trouble himself for him he must study before his rabbi — if so there is no proof from there that in other years those who were not busy came on erev Shabbat. One may say the intent of Hagahot Maimoniyot is that when he said perhaps they are busy with the feast — the intent is not eating the feast, for on that the language "busy" does not apply; also how did Rava sit before Rav Kahana, and Rav Kahana himself — also Rav Assi needed to eat a Purim feast. Although one must hold like Rav Kahana regarding the night meal per Mishnah Ahzaz, nevertheless on Rosh Hashanah Kesha there is a teaching darba dela izd — a meal does not prevent regular study before one's rabbi, and an hour or two of the day suffices for eating needs. Rather R' Eliezer said perhaps they are busy preparing feast needs and R' Eliezer has someone to trouble himself for him. Here one may say R' Eliezer said perhaps they are busy from doubt to judge them favorably. R' Eliezer is difficult either way: if you think they came yesterday on Fast of Esther before Rav Kahana — they had someone to trouble for them, and this is not an excuse that perhaps they are busy; if they did not come yesterday either, on Purim why did they not come today more — he should have wondered yesterday on Fast of Esther why they did not come. If because he holds as seems that if he made the feast at night he fulfilled — therefore yesterday he did not wonder knowing they were busy, unlike by day per his view the bother already passed — what is it that Rava said perhaps they are busy? This excuse is insufficient; rather he should have answered that Rava said a Purim feast made at night did not fulfill. Or at least he should understand there are matters within what he asked why the rabbis did not come. Or even if busy and they have no one to trouble for them — nevertheless they came before their rabbi on Fast of Esther; Purim itself they have time to prepare. What he said perhaps they are busy (and one strains that Purim then fell on Sunday; also possible they ate a little on Motzei Shabbat even though they ate third meal of Shabbat, as Magen Avraham in name of Bach siman 136 seif 1 — from all places they feast at night meal; nevertheless better on day when only 11th falls Thursday as above) — per words of Hagahot Maimoniyot on Purim they were accustomed thus when not busy, proven from Fast of Esther that even busy people came before their rabbi as above.
turei-zahav/2:_: And tomorrow on Friday they fast etc. It does not seem appropriate to rely on this in practice, since Beit Yosef brought in name of Maharam that the fast is moved to Thursday because one cannot postpone until Sunday which is Purim, and likewise one does not fast on erev Shabbat because of honor of Shabbat; and although halacha is established that on erev Shabbat one fasts and completes — that is only when its appointed time comes on erev Shabbat, but when postponed from its time it is not established on erev Shabbat. And as in responsum of Geonim: a communal fast is not fasted — when it is postponed; and Meiri on singular in chapter Kol Marbin: sons of Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava in Tannaita in Tash — what is Ashlomi — for this they said there is torture and complements, and they were used because of Dadoka a name whose time is fixed. What is written in PB Megillat Taanit applies to Fast of Damat and completes — we were in fast of Zabor; nevertheless Rama already wrote in siman 249 a singular Megillat Taanit will not complete, and here it must complete — it will not be fasted in Beit Din, and we will see if Fast of Esther in Beit Din is fulfilled he must complete until stars come out because it is his judgment; so it comes to mind that at his appointed time per sages for Thursday he will not be tormented for milah feast, and on Shabbat he will be tormented until night and Shabbat already entered — what if he is tormented part of Shabbat or all of it? Rather he will eat the milah feast at night as in gemara and siman 12; and here they forbade establishing Fast of Esther on Shabbat because of honor of Shabbat; above siman 249 Rama brought column through people of maaseh to fast on erev Shabbat Shabbat pleasure — their way to eat greedily when fasting; after all most of the world are weak after the fast — therefore the fast should not be established thus.
yad-ephraim/1:_: In Magen Avraham s.k. 3 — see Magen Avraham above siman 17 s.k. 3 in name of Tanhuma and also written in name of Geonim the reason is because they were busy with selichot and could not trouble to honor Shabbat; if so what Rama wrote in Hagahah that it is permitted to eat at milah and on Friday those who ate fast — since selichot and supplications are on Thursday they can well fast on Friday; and Taz challenged Rama — in my humble opinion one may say as I wrote to rely once on Ran, and so Rash and Tur in name of Geonim.
